And said you were scared.\"|That was too much]]}\ <</if>>\ <</if>>\You are not comfortable. That's why you're here. You couldn't stay in that haunted cage anymore. The weighty shadow of sleep retreats quickly. Too quickly. Something's!- {Link [[(Get up!)|Get up!]]}You scramble back like startled prey, knocking over your personal effects, leaning back on your hands, knees bent and heels planted into the ground, ready to leap up and bolt. Everything is still. You wait, panting hard, eyes wide. "Yo." {Link [[(Stay silent.)]]}<<defenceTalk "Broken">> They don't, seem, like a threat. Their tone is genuinely curious. Amused. Your eyes are prepared for the dark. They're sitting. Comfortably. Do not relax. "Why are you here?" {Link [[\"... W-what??\"|What??]]}"In... a basement, in an empty building. Alone. Asleep." <<doubtTalk "Measuring">> Buy time. Get a read. {Link [[\"It's not empty. We're here.\"|It's not empty]]}"Bwahah! Okay, yeah, you're right." You're starting to relax. They have, too. They're not even looking at you, they're focused on nibbling on their digits. {Link [[(Get up, for real.)|Exploring together]]}Your backpack clinks as you show them the more interesting spots you've found over the last few days. You have months of supplies, including the money. It would have been trivial, and lucrative, to rob you. Their thick tail bumps you a few times as they spin by doorways, peeking in at the abandoned contents. They apologise in a different language with each instance. "Less spooky here, together. Kinda homely actually!" <<vulnerabilityTalk "Grazed">> Home. Maybe. {Link [[Continue|Memento]]}"ooOOhh!!" They leap off into a dimly lit room, labelled "props". <<doubtTalk "Poised">> Don't follow. Stay. Wait. Control the situation. {Link [[(Wait.)|Returning with memento]]}They are not quiet as they sneak up to the door, and peek their head around the corner. Soon after, they reveal their plunder: a wooden articulating snake. It rattles slightly as they wiggle it in front of you from its nearly invisible wire. "Memento. To remember this." <<defenceTalk "Waning">> You hadn't realized this was something to remember. You've been too tense to consider it. But you do want to remember this. {Link [[(Take the snake.)]]}<<audio "aFriend" play>>\ The draught here is noticeable, something you're entirely unprepared for. The boat rocks lazily against the meager current, the suggestion of its rope keeping it in place. Its sail has long been taken and repurposed, the motor reclaimed for parts. All that remains is wood too settled for a new home. [[(Board the vessel.)]]{Dialogue}\ <<set $homeTimePassed to $homeTimePassed + 1>>\ A wooden, segmented snake attached to an almost invisible wire. It used to be attached to your wall, as though slithering against gravity. You never gave it the help it needed to get back up. {Option [[(Pick up the snake.)]]}\ {Option [[(Leave the snake.)]]}\ {/Dialogue}\It spans the length of your forearm, and rattles as it moves. You wonder, looking into the tiny glass eyes of this creature made animate, what it has experienced in its life. Who once loved it? Is there anyone who still thinks of it? You can think of at least one other person who might. Its articulation is limited, but effective enough for you to have coiled it around your arm as you think. [[(Return the snake to its perch.)|Return the snake]]Maybe, you were wrong. You don't want to remember this. <<getDialogueOptions "Home options">>\<<set $snakeReturned to true>>\ With a sigh, you lift it to the wall, tie the invisible string to its anchor, drape its body along the metal hooks placed to give it the illusion of life. <<getDialogueOptions "Home options">>\{Dialogue}\ <<set $homeTimePassed to $homeTimePassed + 0>>\ It seems carefree, gliding upwards against gravity. <<getDialogueOptions "Home options">>\ {/Dialogue}\He's climbing the mast, approaching the crow's nest. "Come on! It's sturdy! <span style="font-size:70%">...probably.</span>" <<doubtTalk "Reassured">> It does not seem to mind his weight. Yours will be unnoticeable. [[(Climb the mast.)]]You're not unfit. You still need a moment to regain your breath. The view from here is simply unmatched. Even the ceiling towers of the city center do not have such a clear and unobstructed view of the world. But you can't seem to make out anything. "Wanna jump off? It's deep enough. Promise." <<vulnerabilityTalk "">> Here it is. He's going to kill you. That's all this was. You're going to die, now. {Link [[\"You're trying to kill me.\"|Hesitate jumping]]} {Link [[\"Absolutely not.\"|Hesitate jumping]]} {Link [[\"That's incredibly dangerous.\"|Hesitate jumping]]} {Link [[\"No.\"|Hesitate jumping]]} {Link [[\"I can't swim.\"|Hesitate jumping]]} {Link [[\"Definitely not.\"|Hesitate jumping]]}As you respond, he leaps off, disappearing into the crystal clear water, arcing, resurfacing, splashing. {Link [[\"I can't swim!\"|I can't swim!]]}\Almost no one can, anymore. Things have changed. "I can! Hold your breath, close your eyes. You'll be okay!" [[(Trust.)]]Someone is tapping a song onto your front door. You roll out of bed, still sore. Your backpack, still full, crashes to the floor alongside you. [[(Open the door.)]]At your glare, he briefly stops his rhythmic tapping. Then, quickly, finishes the pattern he had begun. He carries a bag overflowing with tools and materials. You hadn't expected him to take you seriously. {Link [[\"How do you know where I live.\"|How do you know where I live.]]}"I stole your card yesterday. Here you go." He slips your identity back into your pocket as he walks past you. Deftly enough for you to understand how he got it out in the first place. He neatly gathers your papers, maintaining some of your organisation, then begins unloading diamond coated files, coarse paper, blocks of wood, varnish, ... [[(Close the door.)]]He's on your bed, feet kicked up on your wall, head hanging off the edge, looking at you. It's been a long time. Your hands are shaking, you keep plucking mistakes. He doesn't seem to mind. His head tilts to the side as you play the final two notes. "That was nice. Really nice." No one says anything for a while. Memories are ringing. [[(Put the instrument down.)]]You lay your head on your arms, looking out over the water which reaches toward and bends around the forest. You're not really doing anything. The faint breeze from the western egress makes your nose twitch. It's nice. Behind you, he's whittling something that hasn't yet taken form. You should get back to the writing the song. Soon... Soon. Let this last just a bit more. <!--<endRun "Comfortable">-->References back to "Memory of a friend". This is where Coal found you, and saved you from your last dip. It is an old, abandoned theatre. As you explore, you think of the place you were in when Coal found you, what you were recovering from. Perhaps you'll remember other nights the two of you spent in this building. Inspiration notes from wandering my college: Hallways are intermittently lit. The scent of damp, almost sweat. Parts of the ceiling fallen away. Low ceiling, needing to duck at times. Somehow, some ventilation still runs. The faint hum of electricity behind some locked doors. Large, open space. Doors with signs on them: "Up stage, left" "No access" A pipe rushes with the fall of water briefly, then stops. You pretend that revisiting this place will being him back. "Midnight alleys" "Scribes" A basement, that goes deeper. A chain across the walkway. "No access". Distantly, you think you hear steps. "SILENCE" A waiting area, of sorts. Many small doors to the sides of a small space with seats. each door numbered, all locked. It smells vaguely of hummus. The roof arbitrarily changes height each room. Somehow, you feel safer in the dark than the light. Wet floor signs are connectes to walls with webs. The ship you and Coal used to spend time on is in poor condition. If you try to climb the mast as you used to, it will break and throw you into the water. You will never see that view again. You can opt to try to swim to somewhere. Perhaps you give up quickly. Perhaps you succeed with great effort, but don't have the energy to get back.<<heartTalk "High>>It emits a low "thump" as you pull on the handle. It is locked. Coal did not ask before he began cutting a spot for the lock. Once you explained what you had done, there was nothing more to discuss. It was your choice to make, after all. Roughly chiselled into the metal is a small heart, with a question mark in the center. <<if $heart >= 2>>\ <<include [[Are you sure?]]>> <</if>>\<<heartTalk "High">> A ward. You run your finger over its jagged grooves. 'Are you sure?'You can burn your house down, in an attempt to move on from the past. Need a high psyche and low acumen. Set this house on fire. Leave it all behind... Down this route, you need to find somewhere else to stay. Each location you go to have somewhere you can try; Rey's, the abandoned theatre, the old boat, the forest tent. Some places deny you; The Stoat And Magpie.Opening based on the night I connected with Arix. Up late at night, talking about something no one else seemed to understand, listening to the rain.<<if $heart < 1>>\ <<include [[What could you say]]>> <<elseif $heart == 1>>\ <<include [[You haven't been good.]]>> <<else>>\ <<include [[You need him]]>> <</if>>\<!-- This is breaking from the standard structure for my dialogue trees, but I can't see it causing issues. -->\ {Dialogue}\ <<run PlaySong("PartyMusic")>>\ "For now, they're getting things prepared. [[Medium heart]] [[Extreme heart]]<<set $heart to 3>>\ <<goto [[At the party]]>><<set $heart to 1>>\ <<goto [[At the party]]>>I've been feeling bad about the story, lately. I just 'finished' the Party snippet, and I'm just... Unhappy with it. I think a lot of it is coming from comparing my stuff to acloudyskye's stuff, who does pretty much exactly what I want. The music mixed with the characters and animation, it captures precisely how I've felt about events like Arix, with far more subtlety and ease-of-access than I can do. It has maybe inspired me to try doing some of my own 3d renders for the story. I have an idea on what Harbringer might look like - basically enth. But it's a skill that's very far away from me right now. I think visuals are a big part of it. I'm kind of simple, something that looks cute commands a lot of emotions from me. There are no visuals in this, yet. I'd like some, but... I'm not good at it. I'm only one person. I also feel that a lot of my previous writing, compared to the party EC, feels shallow and uninteresting. And that says a lot, when I feel the party is also shallow and uninteresting. I feel like I've limited myself a bit too much with this. A lot of what I love about acloudyskye's world is the freedom and scale of the situation. Exploring a dead world, lots of mystery and uncertainty, few, very close bonds. This story is nearly the opposite of that. You explicitly don't touch the more wonderous side of this setting. It's very mundane, and grounded relatively. That has its merits, but... I wish I could have made the world skye did, I suppose. I wish that about a lot of works. And in a month I might look back on it and see all of its faults. But for now, it's everything I wanted. And I can only see all I don't want, in mine. I'm gonna try to work on other things for a while. College and coding, mostly. Maybe some 3D modelling.
